guides.h1: Fabric cost calculator for Ichalkaranji mills
guides.lead: Ichalkaranji mills cost grey fabric from the same mill-sheet lines every day: reed, pick, counts and rates. Harshvardhan Pareek built fabriccost STUDIO so that sheet becomes a rupee total on the phone — in the shed, not after the shift.

sections.heading: What this calculator is for
paragraphs: A fabric cost calculator for Ichalkaranji is not a generic rupee widget. Powerloom grey fabric is quoted from construction (reed × pick), yarn counts, and the rupee rates the dalal or broker is holding that morning. Miss one line and the total is theatre.

fabriccost STUDIO follows the owner mill notebook used in this cluster: warp weight uses 1825, weft weight uses 1693.33, sizing sits on warp weight, and the dalal line is pick × pick rate. You sign in, name the dalal or broker if you want, then speak or type the sheet.

sections.heading: Who it is for
paragraphs: Jobbers, masters and office staff who already write reed space, L2L, warp count and weft wastage on paper. If you can read a grey-fabric quality, you can fill this studio. Hindi or English speech works in Chrome when you would rather talk than tap.
Harshvardhan Pareek is the maker — based in Ichalkaranji, Maharashtra. The same grey-fabric formulas are used across India; the studio is built around how this town actually costs cloth.

sections.heading: What you enter on the mill sheet
paragraphs: Warp side: reed, warp reed space, L2L, warp count, warp rate and sizing rate. Weft side: pick, weft reed space, weft count, weft rate and wastage percent. Dalal / broker: pick rate. Warping is an optional flat rupee add-on.
Single Warp is one warp yarn and one weft yarn — the classic sheet. Multiple Warp / Weft splits up to three yarns on each side by percentage when the quality is mixed.

sections.heading: Open the studio
paragraphs: The calculator lives on the fabriccost STUDIO homepage. Create a studio account on this device, name the job, and run the sheet. Nothing here promises a search ranking or a market price — only the mill math, clearly accounted for.

guides.keywords: grey fabric costing, warp weft, reed pick, sizing, powerloom, mill sheet, fabriccost STUDIO
guides.h1: Grey fabric costing on a mill sheet
guides.lead: Grey fabric costing is the mill-sheet path from construction and yarn to rupees: warp weight, weft weight, sizing, and the dalal line. fabriccost STUDIO uses the notebook constants — 1825 on warp, 1693.33 on weft — not a fitted shortcut.

sections.heading: Warp weight (1825)
paragraphs: Warp weight = (Reed space × Reed × 120) / (1825 × Warp count × L2L). Reed space and L2L are in the same inch units the shed already uses. The 120 in the numerator is the mill-sheet constant; 1825 in the denominator is the warp constant.
Worked example from the notebook: reed space 65", reed 120, warp count 61, L2L 102. That is (65 × 120 × 120) / (1825 × 61 × 102) = 0.082. That weight is what you multiply by the warp yarn rate.

sections.heading: Weft weight (1693.33)
paragraphs: Weft base = (Reed space × Pick) / (1693.33 × Weft count). Then weft weight = base × (1 + wastage% / 100). Wastage is some percent of that weft base only — the sheet draws the arrow there, not across the whole quality.
The weft line has no L2L. Do not invent one. If the UI shows a weft reed space, that is the reed space that feeds weft weight; warp reed space stays on the warp line.

sections.heading: Sizing, dalal rate, and the total
paragraphs: Sizing = warp weight × sizing rate. It rides on warp weight, not on weft. The dalal / broker line (job rate on older sheets) is pick × pick rate. Warping, when you use it, is a flat rupee add-on.

Grand total = warp cost + weft cost + sizing + dalal line + warping. Warp cost is warp weight × warp rate; weft cost is weft weight × weft rate. Markup percentages on the results screen are a display on that total, not a second mill formula.

howTo.name: How to cost grey fabric from a mill sheet
howTo.description: Turn reed, pick, counts and rates into warp weight, weft weight, sizing and a dalal total.

steps.name: Take reed, reed space, L2L and warp count
steps.text: Compute warp weight as (reed space × reed × 120) / (1825 × warp count × L2L).

steps.name: Take pick, weft reed space, weft count and wastage
steps.text: Compute weft base as (reed space × pick) / (1693.33 × weft count), then add wastage percent on that base only.

steps.name: Apply yarn rates and sizing
steps.text: Multiply warp weight by warp rate and sizing rate. Multiply weft weight by weft rate.

steps.name: Add the dalal line
steps.text: Dalal / broker cost is pick × pick rate. Add optional warping, then read the grand total.

guides.h1: Powerloom fabric cost, from sheet to rupees
guides.lead: Powerloom fabric cost is the rupee total of a grey quality: yarns, sizing and the dalal line. fabriccost STUDIO is built for that sheet — one warp or mixed yarns — so a master can speak the numbers or type them and see every thread accounted for.

sections.heading: Single Warp versus Multiple Warp / Weft
paragraphs: Most powerloom grey qualities are one warp count and one weft count. Single Warp is that classic sheet: one reed, one pick, one rate on each side.

When the quality mixes yarns, Multiple Warp / Weft takes up to three warp slots and three weft slots. Each slot has a percentage, a count and a rate. Each slot takes its share of the same weight formula. The dalal line and warping are not split by yarn percent — they stay on the quality, not the spindle.

sections.heading: Pick rate, dalal, and other rupees
paragraphs: On the mill sheet the making / dalal line is pick × pick rate (dalal rate). That is the job-rate line under another name. Enter the rupees per pick the broker is using; the studio multiplies by pick.

Warping is optional and flat. Results also show a markup table from 5% to 16% on the grand total so you can read a selling conversation without leaving the sheet. Those markups are not a mill law — they are a display on the same total.

sections.heading: Speak or type on the shop floor
paragraphs: Type when the office is quiet. Speak when your hands are on the beam: Chrome Web Speech can stay listening and drop named metrics or numbers in sheet order into in-range fields. Browser voices are optional and stay quiet while you talk. No paid speech key is required.
After Calculate you can edit any field and run the sheet again. That is the point of a powerloom fabric cost tool — correct the pick or the weft rate without rewriting the page.
